chose: writeEnrichment gains an opts:{contentChanged} object, not a positional boolean
because: call sites like writeEnrichment(pool,id,hash,2,labels,true) read as noise; {contentChanged:true} reads as what it does

chose: restate LLM_METHOD_PREFIX locally in load.ts instead of importing llm/schema.ts
because: llm/schema.ts imports zod and was being written concurrently by another agent; load.ts already avoids importing classify.ts for the same reason (classifierVersion is a parameter, not an import) and llmVersion follows the same pattern

chose: on conflict (recipe_id,dimension,slug) do update on BOTH writeEnrichment's and writeLlmEnrichment's inserts
over: delete-then-plain-insert now that the rules delete spares llm:% rows
because: method-scoping means a rules re-run and an LLM write can now target a PK the other provider already owns (llm resolving a rules unknown row, or a later rules re-run recomputing a slug the LLM took over); a plain insert throws 23505 on that PK instead of the FK-only 23503 describeWriteError already handles, and enrich always re-enqueues llm-enrich right after a rules write so a momentary rules-over-llm overwrite self-heals on the next job

chose: markLlmSkipped never stamps llm_version to the current version
over: stamping llm_version=LLM_ENRICHMENT_VERSION on skip, mirroring writeLlmEnrichment's ok write
because: plan §3.1 says a skipped row must be cheap to reset by claiming llm_version < current once the flag turns on; stamping the current version on skip would make that arm never fire again without an explicit force, contradicting the plan's own claimed behavior — leaving llm_version untouched (default 0 for a fresh row) is what makes the non-force reclaim actually happen

chose: claimLlmBatch is a single query joining recipe_enrichment to recipe, no UNION
over: mirroring claimBatch's UNION of 'missing row' and 'out of date row' arms
because: every claimLlmBatch candidate requires status='ok', and a recipe with no recipe_enrichment row can never satisfy that — the inner join alone excludes it, so there is no 'missing row' arm to union in the way the rules claim needs one

chose: writeLlmEnrichment is a plain UPDATE on recipe_enrichment, not an upsert, and throws on 0 rows affected
because: llm-enrich only runs after the rules pass reached status='ok' (plan §9.2 step 3), so a recipe_enrichment row is guaranteed to exist; treating a zero-row update as success would silently leave llm_status claiming never-attempted for a recipe that now has llm: labels, breaking the short-circuit's own invariant

over: add an invariant or boundary claim that the change does not require
because: This slice's real invariants (method-scoped delete, the PK-collision on-conflict on both writeEnrichment and writeLlmEnrichment, markLlmSkipped never stamping llm_version, claimLlmBatch's status='ok' gate) are already pinned as executable load.db.test.ts cases against a real migrated Postgres, not left to prose. Formal anchor/boundary registration in the coherence graph would mean touching graph config files outside the two files I was scoped to (load.ts, load.db.test.ts) and belongs with the coordinator's steps.ts integration, which is the actual chokepoint these functions get wired into.
